pf.license.need: always: each vet holds their own active license from the state's veterinary board
pf.license.who: each vet; each vet tech or assistant only where the state's form licenses, registers or certifies them; the practice too where the state issues a premises or hospital permit, and a mobile practice or unit its own permit where the state's form asks
pf.license.ask: each person's license number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it); the hospital's premises permit and the mobile practice's permit number from the owner, only where the state's form has them
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.controlled_drugs: a switch from the state's form: each vet's federal and state controlled-drug registrations, where the form asks for them at sign-up; Rosie only notes that they're on file and when they end, and never handles drugs, orders or prescriptions
pf.license.boarding: a switch: keeping healthy pets overnight, or grooming them, needs the kennel or boarding license where the state's form asks; the example hospital boards none, so no stays are booked
pf.license.video: a switch from the state's form: video visits only where the state allows them, only for a pet a vet at the practice has examined in person, and only with a vet licensed where the pet is during the visit
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: liability insurance as the business says; shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.shown: the license number shows on the listing and the confirmation where the state's rules require it

pf.safety.stop_action: No booking, and no wait for one. Rosie says: 'This needs a vet now. Go to the nearest emergency animal hospital. The one Lee Animal Hospital works with is open 24 hours.' It gives that hospital's name, address and number, from the owner's settings. For a possible poisoning, it also gives the pet poison line the owner named at sign-up, and says it may charge a fee. Rosie never judges how sick a pet is, and never says what's wrong.
pf.safety.person_danger: the general screen, always on: a person hurt or in danger, like a dog bite to a person, gets 911
pf.safety.go_on: a sick or hurt pet with none of the stop words is booked as a sick or hurt exam, soonest times first; the AI adds: 'If it gets worse, or you see any of these signs, go to the emergency animal hospital now'. Simple first steps, the example practices' own: a small cut gets 'press a clean cloth on it'; a limp gets 'keep your pet quiet'; always 'never give a pet human medicine'. Nothing more: no advice on what's wrong or what to give
pf.safety.worse_before: a text before the visit that the pet seems worse gets the danger check again: a stop word gets the emergency words and flags the hospital; otherwise an earlier time if one is free
pf.safety.bite_risk: a pet that may bite is noted for the team (a muzzle or a calming plan), never a stop

pf.first_steps.records: a new client's records from the last vet: uploaded on the secure page, or the hospital asks the last vet for them (a to-do for the desk, due the day before)
pf.first_steps.on_file: a vaccine visit needs an exam here in the last 12 months; an exam on file is checked for each later booking
pf.first_steps.pre_surgery_exam: surgery and dental cleanings need an exam in the last 30 days first (the example hospital's rule); bloodwork is done the morning of

pf.first_steps.reaction: a pet that had a vaccine reaction last time: the booking waits for the vet's OK
pf.first_steps.new_pet_goodbye: a goodbye visit for a pet the practice hasn't seen: the vet calls the owner first
pf.first_steps.video: a video recheck only for a pet a vet here examined in person

pf.visit.check_in: at the hospital: the check-in code at the front desk; a surgery or dental drop-off: the code at the desk at drop-off, with a number to reach the owner and a pick-up window; at home: the code at the door
pf.visit.estimate: tests and treatment get a written estimate on the secure page (a low and a high, or one total), OK'd before any work; the owner may OK all of it, some lines or none; nothing above the high end without a new yes
pf.visit.found_during_surgery: anything found under anesthesia that isn't on the estimate: the vet calls the owner first; no answer: only what was OK'd is done
pf.visit.drop_off: a drop-off pet gets short updates by text (in, waking up, READY with the pick-up window); the pet goes home only with the code, to the owner or the person named on the page
pf.visit.surgery_not_safe: bloodwork that morning finds it isn't safe today: the vet calls; the bloodwork is charged, and the rest of the deposit is refunded or kept for a new date
pf.visit.results: test results and the diagnosis come only from the vet, by phone or in person, and stay on the secure page, never in a text
pf.visit.goodbye: a quiet room or the family's own home, time with the pet first, sedation first, the owner may stay; no bill at the desk (paid ahead); the pet is marked passed after
pf.visit.done_proof: the check-in code, READY and the pick-up, or DONE; the vet's notes stay in the practice's own records

pf.money.before: nothing taken for exams and vaccine visits; a card saved only where the owner turns on the no-show fee; a deposit for surgery and dental cleanings (the example: $40 for a cat spay; half the estimate's low end otherwise), refunded in full until 24 hours before drop-off; goodbye visits, and a vaccine visit at home, paid in full when booking; nothing kept for a goodbye visit, ever; house calls: the $89 house call fee held
pf.money.after: at the hospital: paid at the front desk, its own way (card, cash, or the hospital's financing); at home: Rosie texts the bill when the vet texts DONE, paid by the saved card or a pay link
pf.money.estimate: the bill is only what the owner OK'd on the estimate; above its high end only with a new yes
pf.money.fees: a no-show or late-cancel fee ($20 at the hospital; up to the $89 house call fee at home), only where the owner turned it on, and only when the owner confirms each one; never for a goodbye visit
pf.money.insurance: pet insurance pays the owner back after the visit: the practice gives the invoice and records for the claim; it doesn't bill the insurer, and Rosie never promises coverage or checks a plan
pf.money.pay_over_time: the practice's own financing choices, its own way; anything else the owner decides
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form
pf.money.tax: the business's tax rate on goods like food and medicines, where the state taxes them (a switch)
pf.money.rosfield_2: Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking applies: a vet isn't a human health practice. For Rosfield's lawyer: do a state's rules against vets sharing fees or paying for referrals reach the $2?
pf.money.plans: a plan's visits are each booked and paid like a single visit (puppy shots at the front desk; a house call plan on the bill Rosie texts); no plan charges a saved card on a set day

pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and the team carry the same, never the reason or results; those stay on the secure page
pf.messages.goodbye: gentle words; nothing sold, no rating, no reminders after; once the pet is marked passed, every text about that pet stops for good, and texts about other pets in the home go on
pf.messages.minors: a teen's request goes to a parent, who books

pf.staff.licenses: each vet's own license, per state; vet techs only where the state's form credentials them; controlled-drug registrations where the state's form asks (a switch)
pf.staff.skills: exams and vaccines (every vet); surgery and dental cleanings (only the vets who do them; here, Marcus); goodbye visits; house calls (here, Owen and Priya for Lee Mobile Vet, and Marcus for the hospital's vaccine visits at home); farm animals (here, Owen)
pf.staff.supervision: vet techs and assistants work under a vet, as the state's rules set (a switch: a vet on site or reachable); anesthesia only with a vet on site
pf.staff.who_oks: the owner OKs a goodbye visit for a pet the practice hasn't seen, same-day exams, estimates over $300 at the hospital and over $500 on a house call (a partner may OK house call prices), fees and refunds
pf.staff.stand_in: another vet may take an exam or a vaccine visit; surgery moves only to another vet who does surgery, or to a new date; a goodbye visit moves to another vet only with the family's yes: with no answer, Sam calls the family, and nothing changes until then

pf.rules.records: the practice keeps medical records as long as the state's rules say; the owner gets a copy within the state's time; a delete removes only Rosie's own booking details
pf.rules.estimate: a switch: a written estimate before treatment where the state's rules require one; the example practices always give one
pf.rules.goodbye_consent: a switch: who may sign a goodbye visit's consent, and whether it's signed with the vet in person; the owner (18 or older) or someone they authorize
pf.rules.video: a switch: video visits only where the state allows them, and only after an in-person exam where it says so
pf.rules.rabies: a switch: rabies vaccine and certificate rules, and the bite question before a goodbye visit, from the state's or the city's form
pf.rules.not_picked_up: a switch: the notice and waiting days the state sets before a pet left after a visit may be placed elsewhere
pf.rules.referral_fees: a switch: where a state's rules bar vets from paying for referrals, Rosfield's lawyer checks the $2 first
pf.rules.license_shown: a switch: the license number on the listing and the confirmation, from the state form
pf.rules.records_years: 7 years for Rosie's own booking records

story.A: Sam Lee, a vet, signs up two companies by text. Then Alex asks for the soonest exam for Biscuit, a dog who is limping, at Lee Animal Hospital. Pick a money choice at the top to follow its path.

notes:
From: dentist. A vet runs like a clinic: exams of a set length with a vet by name, a longer first exam for a new client, the old vet's records as a first step, a written estimate before any test or treatment, results only from the vet, and health details kept on the secure page. Pet words (drop-off, pick-up, READY, a pet that may bite) are borrowed from groomer and boarding; nothing of the dentist's own work is left (check-prof's pilot-word check is at 0).
Names: Sam Lee, a vet, owns Lee Mobile Vet (the master's main company: house calls and farm calls) and Lee Animal Hospital (the second company: the hospital, 410 Birch Ave). Pat is Sam's partner and OKs Lee Mobile Vet prices over $500.
People: at the hospital Marcus (vet, the only surgeon) and Nadia (vet); on the mobile team Owen (vet, also farm animals) and Priya (vet). Alex M. stays the customer. Pets: Biscuit (a limping Lab, the main story A), Luna (A's cat spay path), Rufus (A's goodbye path), Pepper (an older cat, the main story B), Daisy (B's goodbye path). The master's customer Owen H. became Felix, so the two Owens never meet.
Kinds of work: plumbing became mobile vet care (house calls), electrical became farm care (it waits for Owen's license), the barbershop became the animal hospital.
Prices are the example practices' own, not a standard: sick exam $72 (Biscuit's estimate $461 in all), vaccine visit $35 at the hospital or $75 at home, recheck $40 (free within 14 days for the same problem), nail trim $20, puppy shots $35 a visit as a plan, cat spay $140 ($40 deposit), dental cleaning from the exam's estimate (deposit half its low end), goodbye visit $185 at the hospital and $385 at home, paw print $25, private cremation $150; house call fee $89, wellness exam and vaccines at home $179, sick pet at home priced at the visit ($245 in the example), senior bloodwork at home $199; the hospital's no-show fee $20, off unless Sam turns it on.
Money A (all at the hospital, paid at the front desk its own way): visit|none|counter is the main path (a sick or hurt exam: only the $72 exam promised, a written estimate before any test). list|none|counter is a vaccine visit (a YES books it). list|card|counter is the same visit where Sam turns on the $20 no-show fee: a card is saved only for it. list|deposit|counter is the $140 cat spay: a $40 deposit before surgery under anesthesia, the rest at pick-up. list|full|none is the $185 goodbye visit, paid when booking so the family never stops at the desk. Left out: holds, photos, Rosfield's bill or card charge (the hospital has a front desk).
Money B (house calls): visit|hold|bill is the main path (a sick cat at home: the $89 house call fee held, Owen's estimate OK'd before tests, Rosie texts the bill). list|hold|bill is the $179 wellness exam and vaccines at home. list|full|none is the $385 goodbye visit at home, paid when booking, in a 2-hour arrival window. Left out: photos (a vet never prices from photos), deposits and saved-card charges at home, own-way billing. The tip branch (B9-19) is off: pf.money.tips is none.
The sign-up example sets money only the vet's way: S1-13 to S1-16 (house calls held, goodbye paid in full) and S1-41 to S1-47 (the hospital's list, nothing taken, the spay deposit, the goodbye paid in full, the vaccine at home $75 paid in full). Each sign-up step on flow A reads the same on every money path.
Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking applies, paid by the business: a vet isn't a human health practice. For Rosfield's lawyer (pf.money.rosfield_2, pf.rules.referral_fees): do a state's rules against vets sharing fees or paying for referrals reach the $2?
Privacy: the diagnosis, test results, and medicine names or doses stay on the secure page, never in a text, to the owner or the team. Texts name the pet, the vet, the visit kind, the date, time, place, price and a secure link; staff text 'notes on the page'.
Danger: the vet's stop words (trouble breathing, a possible poisoning, can't stand, bloat signs, a seizure, bleeding, a cat that can't pee, trouble giving birth) send the owner at once to the nearest emergency animal hospital, the one Sam named at sign-up (S1-22), with a pet poison line for a poisoning (it may charge a fee). Never a booking, never a wait. Rosie never judges how sick a pet is and never diagnoses. A pet that seems worse before the visit gets the check again (A7-13, B7-17).
Licenses: each vet's own; vet techs and assistants only where the state's form credentials them; the hospital's premises permit and a mobile practice permit where the state issues them; controlled-drug registrations only noted where the state's form asks (Rosie handles no drugs). Video visits and boarding are switches from the state's form. No single state or city is named anywhere.
Goodbye visits are fee-free in both flows: no warning, no late or no-show fee, a full refund or a move, nothing sold (only what the family asks for, like a paw print, priced first), no rating, and the pet marked passed so no text about it goes out again. The master's fee steps and what-ifs don't vary by service, so the overlay gives each one a goodbye-path variant (A7-06 to A7-10, A8-14 to A8-22, A8-46, A8-57 to A8-64, A10-07, A10-08, A10-25, A10-32, A10-33, B7-10, B7-14, B8-10, B8-16, B8-60, B8-66, B10-18, B10-25 and others). That is gap 'Sensitive visits, and a death'.
What-ifs that named the main story's pet get the right pet on the other paths (Luna on the spay path, Rufus and Daisy on the goodbye paths), so a goodbye path never sells vaccines or sends results.
Off: flow A's plan and insurance branches (pet insurance pays the owner back), a day-before hold failing (the hospital holds nothing), an item not picked up and rented items (A10-06), a child going home (A8-32), walk-in seats and tables; flow B's photo, landlord, plan, tip, sent-now (no on-call house calls), nobody-home, delivery, outside-check, item-to-the-shop and permit-inspection branches. Each off says why.
Plug-in splits kept (splitsKept A): A4-43 first step (records, an exam on file, the anesthesia consent), A7-61 stand-in with the skill (only Marcus does surgery), A8-02 what to bring, A8-53 a drop-off, A10-34 a rating (never after a goodbye visit; B10-02 gets the same as its own branch).
Clocks run forward on every listed path; words ops set 't' only where the master's time didn't fit (Owen's estimate at 8:40am, B8-20).
Not sure: whether a state lets a vaccine visit be given at home by a hospital (S1-43 checks it); whether the goodbye consent must be signed with the vet in person (a switch); the 14-day free recheck and the 24-hour spay deposit refund are the example practices' own policies.
Review (Oct 23): goodbye paths now ask once more before a cancel, never cut a late family short, never move to another vet without the family's yes (Sam calls), and never ask the family whether a visit happened (Rosie asks the vet). Plans charge no saved card (A7-02 and B7-05 plan-charge branches off; pf.money.plans). Section 11's recheck takes nothing at booking on the paths that take nothing. Sam names a pet poison line at sign-up (S1-22).
Refit Oct 27 2026 (R13) to the REDESIGN 2 master: facts animals, dropoff, firststeps, forms, results, video, aftercare; no switches (pet care is not sensitive work; the $2 stays); A set start times, B arrival windows, free cancel until 24 hours before. The $89 house call fee is no longer held (D66): on the visit path it's the fee owed even after a no to the estimate (B4-14), on the list path the saved card's late-cancel or nobody-home fee; goodbye visits keep nothing (fee $0). Every legacy words op dropped; own words only on S1-13 (the money card, both flows). Kept words: 'leak' (a privacy leak), 'visit fee' (the master's rule for a price set at the visit), 'house call' (the vet's own word), 'cleaning' (B3-13's wrong-number call to a dental office, the master's example).
